articles.title: Instagram posts in Klaviyo/Mailchimp without Zapier tax
articles.excerpt: You want the latest Instagram posts in a welcome series or a weekly brand email. The “easy” path is usually a Zap: new Instagram post → somehow → Mailchimp / Klaviyo. It works until the task meter spi…
articles.body: You want the latest Instagram posts in a welcome series or a weekly brand email. The “easy” path is usually a Zap: new Instagram post → somehow → Mailchimp / Klaviyo. It works until the task meter spikes, the Zap breaks on a Meta permission change, or someone asks why the images in last month’s send are blank. There is a quieter option most email tools already support: a feed URL. Paste it into a native RSS block (Mailchimp) or a web feed (Klaviyo). No Zap. No Make scenario. No third widget whose free tier pauses when a campaign goes semi-viral. We built Feedframer for that path — among others. This is the email-shaped write-up: how it works, what it costs next to Zapier, and the trade-offs we will not paper over.

articles.title: Node.js Marketplace Moderation: Multi-Model Gateway and Direct Provider Billing Estimates
articles.excerpt: Short answer: A Vercel gateway, OpenRouter, or direct provider can serve this Node.js workflow; the defensible route preserves a normalized moderation record, meets the deadline, and exposes usage evi…
articles.body: Short answer: A Vercel gateway, OpenRouter, or direct provider can serve this Node.js workflow; the defensible route preserves a normalized moderation record, meets the deadline, and exposes usage evidence. A Node.js app should compare a Vercel gateway, OpenRouter, and a direct provider route by measured quality, deadline, and telemetry completeness. The cheapest route is not a gateway choice; it is the route that avoids a second classification, a human recheck caused by missing evidence, and an unbounded stream of high-cardinality logs. For an e-commerce marketplace, the useful unit is one moderation report: text, policy context, model decision, confidence, and an audit reference. I would keep that contract stable across direct provider calls and gateways.

articles.title: GEAR: How Feature-Based Code Generation Abstracts Away Multi-Agent Framework Lock-In
articles.excerpt: Every multi-agent builder hits the same wall: you pick LangGraph for its state machine, then realize CrewAI's task delegation fits your use case better, or AutoGen's conversational patterns match your…
articles.body: Every multi-agent builder hits the same wall: you pick LangGraph for its state machine, then realize CrewAI's task delegation fits your use case better, or AutoGen's conversational patterns match your domain. Switching means rewriting orchestration logic, tool registration, and memory plumbing from scratch. GEAR (a fresh ArXiv paper, 2610.35592v1) proposes a framework-agnostic configuration layer that generates working agent system code across ten frameworks from a single feature specification. The promise is portability. The cost is lowest-common-denominator constraints and framework-specific adaptation reports you need to read before deploying.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.

articles.excerpt: A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure, which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and me…
articles.body: BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure , which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base, will keep the infrared space telescope cool as it searches for near-Earth asteroids and comets while also providing the spacecraft with power. When in space, NEO Surveyor will detect some of the hardest-to-find asteroids and comets, some of which may be located in the direction of the Sun — a region of sky where ground-based optical telescopes have a harder time searching. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 27, 1961: NASA launches Saturn I rocket on 1st test flight from Florida to set stage for the mighty Saturn V moon rocket
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. The Saturn I rocket was the United States' first heavy-lift rocket designed to launch big payloads beyond low Earth orbit. This was also the first test flight of any rocket in the Saturn family of rockets, which includes the Saturn V that was used to launch astronauts to the moon during the Apollo program . The Saturn I was enormous compared to every rocket that came before it. It was almost three times as tall as the Jupiter-C rocket, which launched the first American satellite into orbit in 1958. It also produced more than 10 times the amount of thrust that the Jupiter-C rocket could. The liquid-powered rocket launched on its maiden voyage from Cape Canaveral.
